s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of left leg pain and weakness with associated systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Increasing left leg pain and weakness
key_facts: 87-year-old man with multiple comorbidities
One week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
Impaired mobility
Single episode of urinary incontinence
Anorexia and 12% body-weight loss over six months
Blood pressure 88/45 mmHg
Heart rate 96/min
Temperature 36.4 °C
Oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Weight 51 kg (BMI 19 kg/m2)
Neurologic examination showed 4/5 strength in left hip and knee flexors and extensors
Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
Pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
Mild foraminal narrowing at L5–S1 on MRI of the lumbar spine
No central canal stenosis or abscess
Left hip pain worsened despite analgesia
Strength declined to 2/5 at the hip and 3/5 at the knee
CRP and ESR continued to rise

shortlist.label: Psoas abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers, left hip pain, and muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Worsening left hip pain, joint effusion, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers, left hip pain, and muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
shortlist.why_kept: Acute to subacute onset of left leg pain and weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and associated systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute to subacute onset of left leg pain and weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and associated systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of increasing left leg pain and weakness, impaired mobility, and elevated inflammatory markers, along with the finding of bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement on MRI, is most consistent with a psoas abscess. The absence of central canal stenosis or abscess on the lumbar spine MRI and the lack of evidence for septic arthritis or osteomyelitis on imaging and laboratory tests further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: No evidence of joint infection on imaging or laboratory tests

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: No evidence of bone infection on imaging or laboratory tests

rejected.label: Polymyalgia rheumatica
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are more consistent with a localized infection rather than a systemic inflammatory condition

rejected.label: Giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: The patient's age and symptoms are not typical for giant cell arteritis, and there is no evidence of temporal artery involvement
